title: AuthZ Sentinel: policy cache + runtime interceptor for API & Console
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a lightweight, horizontally-scalable authorization layer (AuthZ Sentinel) that provides low-latency policy evaluation and pluggable middleware for API gateway, runtime inference path, and Redwood Console. The system will: (1) index RBAC v2 policies into a compact in-memory structure optimized for fast checks, (2) expose a small evaluator library usable as a local sidecar or embedded runtime hook, (3) maintain a bounded policy cache with versioning and invalidation hooks, and (4) surface rich audit events for compliance and troubleshooting. The design emphasizes predictable p99 authz latency (<10ms), high cache hit rates (>90% for steady-state), safe rollouts with canary and fallback to a conservative deny/allow policy, and minimal coupling to SSO/SAML attribute mapping logic. This ticket covers design, PoC evaluator, middleware adapters (HTTP/gRPC/console), audit event schema, telemetry, and rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: A compact policy indexer that converts RBAC v2 rules to runtime predicates and produces a versioned policy blob
Evaluator library with a stable API for allow|deny|explain and a median authz check latency under 3ms in microbenchmarks
Middleware adapters for API gateway (HTTP), runtime inference path (interceptor), and Console (React+backend guard) that call the evaluator synchronously and emit audit events
Cache semantics documented: TTL, explicit invalidation on policy change, and per-tenant isolation; tests cover stale policy cases
End-to-end integration tests exercising SAML->role mapping to RBAC v2 rules and showing correct enforcement for admin/regular roles
Telemetry dashboards with authz latency percentiles, cache hit rate, per-tenant denied count, and correlated audit log sampling
Security review completed and sign-off from security@g.redwood.ai; demo in weekly infra sync
updates: 2025-01-15: Kickoff meeting with Security, Platform, and DX. Agreed on 'Sentinel' naming and that evaluator must be embeddable (C++/Go) and have a thin HTTP sidecar shim for language portability.

2025-01-22: Completed spike comparing policy representation formats (AST vs decision table vs bloom-index). Chose compact predicate index + small forwarding table to reduce evaluator branching and memory overhead.

2025-01-30: PoC evaluator implemented in Go (internal repo branch feature/authz-sentinel). Microbenchmarks: median 1.9ms, p99 7.8ms for a synthetic workload with 10k rules; memory footprint ~12MB per tenant index.
2025-02-04: Design review feedback from Platform: add strict mode toggle to fail-closed vs fail-open on unexpected errors; added in design doc link.

2025-02-10: Middleware adapter prototypes: HTTP interceptor for API gateway; gRPC interceptor for runtime; backend guard hook for Console. All adapters emit audit events to the audit-sink topic with schema v0.1.

2025-02-14: Benchmarks on k8s test cluster with 4 replicas: steady load 20k auth checks/sec with average latency 2.6ms; cache hit rate 93% using 60s TTL for user-role lookups. Recorded regressions when policies contain >50 dynamic conditions per rule.

2025-02-18: Security requested explicit explainability fields for denied decisions for SOC investigations. Added 'explain' output in evaluator API and audit event. Raising potential data exposure risk; security suggested redaction rules for explain payloads.

2025-02-21: Preparing PR for evaluator core (GH: redwood-inference/authz-sentinel PR#92) and middleware adapters (GH PR#98). Planning canary rollout for runtime-2.4 in staging next week. Drafting runbook for policy invalidation edge cases.
notes: Trade-offs considered: full Rego/OPA vs minimal evaluator. Chosen minimal evaluator to guarantee p99 latency and simple integration with existing runtime containers. If policy expressiveness limits surface, we will add a translation step from higher-level policy DSL to predicates.

Cache model: per-tenant in-memory LRU + version tag. On policy publish, control plane emits a policy-change event to policy-stream; sentinel sidecars subscribe and atomically swap index with new version. This gives eventual consistency but bounded staleness and simple rollback semantics.

SSO/SAML: mapping layer will normalize SAML attributes into role assertions and custom claims. Mapping table lives in admin console and publishes mapping as part of the versioned policy blob. Edge case: transient identity provider errors should not break eval; middleware must be able to reference last-known mapping with TTL.

Audit: event includes timestamp, requester id, resolved principal, policy_version, decision, explain (redactable), resource, action, route, tenant_id. Events are written to Kafka audit-sink and to object storage snapshots for long-term retention for customers who enable compliance add-on.

Operational controls: admin console will expose policy diff view, 'simulate' mode for testing policy changes against sample traffic, and one-click rollback. RBAC UI must be gated by SSO admin role and MFA-required toggle for policy changes.

Fallback behavior: default policy for unknown tenants is deny-by-default. For legacy tenants opting into migration, we will enable a permissive compatibility flag and emit verbose audit entries to identify missing rules.
Performance targets: p50 <3ms, p95 <6ms, p99 <12ms for authz checks under typical load; target cache hit rate >90% for tenant-user lookups in production after warmup.
